correctness.rationale: On Hermitian matrices, i[H,X] is skew with respect to real Hilbert–Schmidt pairing, so homogeneous response energy forces boundary diagonals and every off-diagonal zero; bond equations then force all diagonals zero, establishing invertibility. Diagonal equations yield conserved j and X_11=1/2−j/Γ, X_NN=−1/2+j/Γ. Pairing with X yields source Γ/2−j and dissipative energy 2Γ(1/2−j/Γ)^2+[γ(N−1)+Γ]j²/(2t²)+E; rearrangement gives j(1−j/j0)=E≥0. j=0 contradicts source boundary values and zero coherences. E=0 kills real nearest-neighbor and all longer coherences; real bond equations then force v_k−v_{k+1}=0. A directly constructed constant-potential response attains equality. Independently solved N=3, t=Γ=γ=1, v=(0,1,2): j=6/25,j0=2/7,E=24/625. Entire check code inspected; all-N proof is the dissipative identity, not finite tests.
